name: Leather fragrances

card.summary: Smoky, birch-tar and suede-style scents that people wear to add a rugged, polished scent signature to their overall presentation.
card.note: Scent perception is personal and fragrance can irritate sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
Leather fragrances are perfumes and colognes built around a leather accord, often smoky and dry, traditionally associated with birch tar and woods. People wear them to round out a look with a scent that reads as rugged or refined.

The best-known historical example is Chanel's Cuir de Russie from 1927. Forum discussion of cologne in general describes scent as part of attracting others, but there are no studies on leather scents specifically.
quick.how: Worn like any fragrance, applied to skin or clothing as part of grooming. Some people choose leather scents for evening or cooler weather and layer them with other notes of wood or spice.
quick.risks: Fragrance can cause skin irritation or allergy in some people, and scent preference varies widely between individuals.

lead: A leather fragrance is a perfume whose central accord evokes the smell of leather, frequently smoky and dry in character. A well-documented early example is Chanel's Cuir de Russie (1927), created by perfumer Ernest Beaux, which the house describes as evoking the smell of boots tanned with birch bark [2].

People use these scents as part of grooming: fragrance is a finishing detail of presentation alongside clothing and hair. On T Nation, one poster wrote that he had avoided cologne as effeminate but now wore it, citing a belief that smell is tied to memory and that women like it [1].
No clinical studies have tested leather scents themselves.

chain: Adds a rugged or refined scent signature
angle.text: Wearers use leather fragrances to add a distinctive, masculine-leaning scent signature to their overall presentation. The appeal is stylistic and personal rather than something measured.

paras: Leather-note perfumes are named for the smell of leather. Chanel's Cuir de Russie, composed by Ernest Beaux and released in 1927, is the page's best-known case; its notes include bergamot, rose, jasmine, juniper wood, sandalwood and amber alongside a smoky leather character [2].

Fragrance appears in men's style discussions as one more grooming element. A 2015 T Nation thread on men's fashion includes a poster who says wearing cologne is justified because scent activates memory and women respond to it, while also admitting he once saw it as effeminate [1].

timeline.event: Chanel releases Cuir de Russie, composed by Ernest Beaux [2].

lore.intro: Cologne in general is discussed on strength-training forums as a grooming detail [1].

claims.claim: Cologne affects how women perceive a man
claims.believers: A T Nation poster cites memory and attraction effects as reasons he wears cologne [1].
claims.experts: No studies on leather fragrances were reviewed for this entry.
